Corpus › Functions & modules › import

import

Translation status: English reader-locale proof. Term names and code fences follow the en pack; supporting prose may still be English.

Imports names from another module or package source.

Aliases: import

Syntax: import from <source> [public] (<name> [as <alias>] | * as <alias>)

Category#

package

Related#

  • from
  • private
  • annotation-sugar

Examples#

radix/corpus/importa/default-braced.fab (canonical · keyword)#

Canonical braced import record with private binding inferred from the path.

# =============================================================================
# import — Canonical braced import record with private binding inferred from the path
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Canonical braced import record with private binding inferred from the path.
#   • Related keywords: from, private, annotation-sugar
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Letting the compiler infer an import name that collides with an existing top-level binding — use `name` or `as` to disambiguate (SEM005).
#
# See also: from, private, annotation-sugar
# =============================================================================

# import — canonical braced record
#
# The canonical record spells the source field and lets visibility/name defaults
# materialize the same ImportDecl as `import from "norma:text"`.

import { from = "norma:text" }

print "importa-braced"

Expected output:

importa-braced

radix/corpus/importa/importa.fab (canonical · keyword)#

Imports names from another module or package source.

# =============================================================================
# import — Imports names from another module or package source
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Imports names from another module or package source.
#   • Related keywords: from, public, as
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • Missing the `from` source in the import record — an import record requires an `from` source path.
#
# See also: from, public, as
# =============================================================================

# import from — named import from a sibling module
#
# import from relative path; an absent marker does not re-export.
#
# GRAMMAR:
#   import from "<path>" <name> [as <alias>]
#   import from "<path>" public <name>   (re-export)
#
# Requires module layout: import/importa.fab imports from import/auxilium.fab.
# Harness compiles single files in isolation — sibling resolution needs package
# or module mode (faber check --package), not bare single-file emit.
#
# EXPECTED OUTPUT:
#   "Salve, Marcus!" on successful link.
#
# BACKEND: Rust/Go e2e whitelist — single-file compile cannot resolve sibling.

import from "./auxilium" auxilium

main {
    print auxilium.saluta("Marcus")
}

Expected output:

Salve, Marcus!

radix/corpus/importa/braced-field-english-reject-la.fab (supporting · reject)#

The English record field word from in a la file is an unknown import field (expect parse error).

# =============================================================================
# import — English record field word in a la file (expect parse error)
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Locale surfaces are sealed in both directions — the la spelling of the
#     source field is `from`, so the English `from` is not a field of a la record
#   • Parse error — `PARSE050:unknown_import_field` lists the la field words
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • writing `from`, `visibility`, `name`, `as` or `all` in a la record —
#     write `from`, `visibility`, `name`, `as` or `all`
#
# See also: import, from
# =============================================================================

# English record field word in a la file (expect parse error)
#
# DELIBERATE: this exemplum keeps the English field word (`from`) on purpose, to
# pin the PARSE050 `unknown_import_field` diagnostic in a la file.

import { from = "norma:text" }

print "unreachable"

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/importa/braced-field-latin-reject.fab (supporting · reject)#

The Latin record field word from in an en file is a wrong-locale error (expect parse error).

# =============================================================================
# import — Latin record field word in an en file (expect parse error)
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   • Locale surfaces are sealed — the en spelling of the source field is
#     `from`, so the Latin `from` is refused in an en file
#   • Parse error — `PARSE050:wrong_locale_import_field` names the word written
#     and the en word to use instead
#
# Common mistakes:
#   • writing `from`, `visibility`, `name`, `as` or `all` in an en record —
#     write `from`, `visibility`, `name`, `as` or `all`
#
# See also: import, from
# =============================================================================

# Latin record field word in an en file (expect parse error)
#
# DELIBERATE: this exemplum keeps the Latin field word (`from`) on purpose, to pin
# the PARSE050 `wrong_locale_import_field` diagnostic.

import { from = "norma:text" }

print "unreachable"

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/importa/import-missing-member-reject.fab (supporting · reject)#

A wildcard alias reaches only the members its module exports; calling a member the module never exports is a typecheck reject.

# =============================================================================
# import - an alias reaches the module's exported surface, nothing else
# =============================================================================
#
# What this teaches:
#   - `* as L` binds the exported surface of the sibling module: `L.greet`
#     resolves, `L.absent` names nothing the module exports.
#   - A call through a namespace alias to a member the imported file does not
#     export is `namespace_missing_export` (SEM004), reported at the call.
#
# Common mistakes:
#   - Expecting the alias to re-export module-private names: those are
#     `import_module_private` (SEM006), a different seam.
#
# See also: import, public, as
# =============================================================================

# import missing member - the alias reaches only exported members
#
# GRAMMAR:
#   import from "./lib" * as L
#
# Requires module layout: import-missing-member-reject.fab imports lib.fab
# (package or module mode).
#
# EXPECTED: SEM004:namespace_missing_export - `absent` is not on lib's
# exported surface (lib.fab exports greet, K and Pt only).

import from "./lib" * as L

main {
    print L.absent("x")
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/importa/import-unknown-norma-module-reject.fab (supporting · reject)#

Importing a norma:* module name that the embedded library does not provide is a package-graph reject.

# This exemplum intentionally fails to compile: `norma:nonexistent` names no
# module of the embedded Norma library, so package analysis rejects the import.
import from "norma:nonexistent" nonexistent

main {
    print "unreachable"
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/importa/private-reject.fab (supporting · reject)#

An unmarked top-level member of an imported module is module-private.

# =============================================================================
# import — a module-private member is not reachable through the import
# =============================================================================
# `hidden` carries no `@ public`, so it belongs to `lib` alone. Reaching it
# through the module binding is a semantic error, not a name that falls back to
# a module-local definition.

import from "./lib" lib

main {
    print lib.hidden()
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.

radix/corpus/importa/selective-missing-reject.fab (supporting · reject)#

A selective import must name a member the imported module exports.

# =============================================================================
# import — a selective import names an exported member
# =============================================================================
# `nosuch` is not on `lib`'s exported surface (`@ public`), and it is not a
# module-private name either: a selective binding that names nothing the module
# exports is its own error, reported at the import.

import from "./lib" const nosuch

main {
    print 1
}

Expected: compilation rejects this example.
